title: IELTS Academic 19 - Listening Test 4 - Part 3
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 3

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

13:15ANNOUNCER: Part three. You will hear two students called Jane and Kieran talking about books.
13:22ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
14:02ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
14:11KIERAN: So Jane – you'll be off to Denmark soon to do your work placement.
14:14JANE: Yes, I'm really looking forward to it and I've just started packing up all my books to put in storage.
14:22KIERAN: Well, I hope they don't get spoilt.
14:24JANE: It's OK – my grandfather works in a bookshop and he told me how to pack them.
14:30KIERAN: Oh, that's helpful.
14:31JANE: He says you have to support the spine otherwise the paper can come away from the cover.
14:37KIERAN: Yeah – that's obvious.
14:39JANE: He also told me to pack them flat in the box not on their side – again because they can bend and if you leave them like that for, say, a year, it's quite hard to get them back to their normal shape.
14:53KIERAN: Well, it's pretty clear that ruins them, but a lot of people just can't be bothered to protect their books.
14:59JANE: He always says it's such a shame that publishers don't use better-quality paper. It's the acid in the paper that causes the problem, isn't it?
15:08KIERAN: Yeah – that's why old books go yellow. You know some of the books my grandfather's given me are like that already.
15:16JANE: Oh... I should dump them really if they're going to deteriorate further, but I'd feel bad. They'll always remind me of him. He's quite a collector, you know.
15:27KIERAN: Well, if they're important to you...
15:28JANE: Yeah – I'd regret just throwing them away. You know, maybe it's because I was taught to treasure books... but I hate seeing students force open the pages – of paperbacks. They press so hard they end up breaking the spine.
15:43KIERAN: I know, but unfortunately, paperbacks aren't designed to last a long time and people know that. Hardbacks aren't quite as weak.
15:52JANE: Yeah, they're different, I suppose. But I still don't think people value hardbacks like they used to.
15:59KIERAN: Well, they aren't decorative, are they, like other objects. Plus, nowadays, people don't keep them out on shelves as much as they used to. That's such a pity. When I visit someone – if they have, say, a colourful book on a table, it's the first thing I'm drawn to. JANE: I agree – and book covers can be a work of art in themselves. Some are really eye-catching.
16:25KIERAN: I've always been taught to handle books carefully. If you watch someone take a book off a shelf, well, they usually do it wrong.
16:34JANE: Ah, my grandfather says, you should put your hand right over the top of the book... or if you can't do that, pull the other books on the shelf aside so that you can hold the whole cover.
16:46KIERAN: When did you learn all this?
16:48JANE: He watched me pull a heavy book off the shelf when I was small, and it fell on the floor and broke apart.
16:55KIERAN: Oh dear!
16:56JANE: I can still remember it! You know what I really like?
17:00KIERAN: What?
17:01JANE: The smell of new books.
17:03KIERAN: Me too. My parents used to laugh at me when I was a kid because I loved putting books up to my nose. Almost as much as reading them!
17:10JANE: New books aren't cheap, though, are they? KIERAN: I guess we're lucky we can buy them. My grandfather stocks second-hand books as well as new ones and they don't smell quite as good.
17:25ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.
17:57ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
18:05KIERAN: I'd love to have a bookshop like your grandfather. What's it like?
18:09JANE: Well, it's quite big – it's got two floors and an attic, and he stocks all kinds of books really.
18:18KIERAN: I guess he treasures things like first editions and other rare books.
18:22JANE: Yeah – you might think he'd keep those in the attic or somewhere.
18:26KIERAN: ... so they'd be hidden?
18:28JANE: Yeah. But he likes people to know that he has them. So, he puts them out in the shop but makes sure you need a ladder to get them.
18:37KIERAN: Right. That would prevent any thefts!
18:39JANE: Uh-huh.
18:40KIERAN: Does he stock books for children?
18:42JANE: He does. He particularly likes to encourage kids to read; he always says that he used to sit under the stairs as a child with a pile of books and read them all.
18:54KIERAN: Is that where he keeps them, then?
18:55JANE: Not exactly – he's got a dedicated area on the ground floor with cushions so that parents can enter with their toddlers, go there and spend some time reading to them.
19:07KIERAN: Oh cool.
19:08JANE: And then there's a place for pushchairs by the front door. And a café if anyone needs refreshments.
19:14KIERAN: That's good to know.
19:16JANE: As I said, it's a big shop and there's a storage area out the back as well.
19:21KIERAN: Oh, what does he keep there? Books he wants to throw away?
19:25JANE: He hardly ever throws anything away – he just leaves unwanted books by the front door for customers to take.
19:32KIERAN: Well, that's very nice.
19:35JANE: Yeah – and books people or institutions have requested, they all go at the far end.
19:41KIERAN: Oh.
19:42JANE: He thinks it's best to keep these out of the main shopping area as they're boxed and new.
19:48KIERAN: Did you get your coursebooks from him?
19:50JANE: Naturally. He stocks books for a lot of the colleges. He used to keep these books on the first floor, but now there's a new university in my hometown, he's moved them downstairs to attract the students. They're actually part of the coffee shop on low shelves all around it.
20:08KIERAN: Pretty central then. You'll have to take me there some time!
20:15ANNOUNCER: That is the end of part 3. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to part 3.

groups.title: Questions 26–30
groups.instructions:
Where does Jane's grandfather keep each of the following types of books in his shop?
Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–G, next to Questions 26–30.

options.text: at the back of the shop

q21.text: Kieran thinks the packing advice given by Jane's grandfather is

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (common sense)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'He says you have to support the spine... KIERAN: Yeah - that's obvious.'
• 'that's obvious' (điều hiển nhiên) đồng nghĩa với 'common sense'.

q22.text: How does Jane feel about the books her grandfather has given her?
options: A. They are not worth keeping.
B. They should go to a collector.
C. They have sentimental value for her.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (They have sentimental value for her)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'I'd feel bad. They'll always remind me of him. He's quite a collector...'
• Những cuốn sách gợi nhớ về người ông nên có giá trị kỷ niệm (sentimental value).

q23.text: Jane and Kieran agree that hardback books should be
options: B. given as gifts to visitors.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (put out on display)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'people don't keep them out on shelves as much... a colourful book on a table, it's the first thing I'm drawn to. JANE: I agree...'
• Cả hai đều đồng ý nên trưng bày sách bìa cứng trên bàn hoặc kệ.

q24.text: While talking about taking a book from a shelf, Jane
options: A. describes the mistakes other people make doing it.
B. reflects on a significant childhood experience.
C. explains why some books are easier to remove than others.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (reflects on a significant childhood experience)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'He watched me pull a heavy book off the shelf when I was small, and it fell on the floor and broke apart. I can still remember it!'
• Kỷ niệm thời thơ ấu (childhood experience) khi cô ấy làm rơi sách vỡ gáy.

q25.text: What do Jane and Kieran suggest about new books?
options: A. Their parents liked buying them as presents.
B. They would like to buy more of them.
C. Not everyone can afford them.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (Not everyone can afford them)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'New books aren't cheap, though, are they? KIERAN: I guess we're lucky we can buy them.'
• Sách mới không hề rẻ và họ thấy may mắn mới mua được = không phải ai cũng có khả năng chi trả (afford).
• Đáp án đúng: D (on a high shelf)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'he puts them out in the shop but makes sure you need a ladder to get them.'
• Cần dùng thang (ladder) để lấy sách quý hiếm -> sách để trên kệ cao (on a high shelf).
• Đáp án đúng: F (in a specially designed space)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'he's got a dedicated area on the ground floor with cushions so that parents can enter with their toddlers...'
• 'dedicated area with cushions' = in a specially designed space.
• Đáp án đúng: A (near the entrance)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'he just leaves unwanted books by the front door for customers to take.'
• 'by the front door' = near the entrance.
• Đáp án đúng: C (at the back of the shop)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'books people or institutions have requested, they all go at the far end.'
• 'at the far end' = at the back of the shop.
• Đáp án đúng: G (within the café)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'They're actually part of the coffee shop on low shelves all around it.'
• 'part of the coffee shop' = within the café.
